title: 3D/4D ultrasound in pregnancy
what: It is a normal pregnancy ultrasound, but the image is three-dimensional. In 4D, you can see your baby move in real time.
why: Most often because parents want it. Sometimes the doctor uses 3D to see certain organs of the baby better.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; photos and videos are given right away
tell_doctor: Results of past ultrasounds and screenings
If something worries you: pain or discharge

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The baby's face is usually best seen between 24 and 32 weeks. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: No special preparation. You can have a snack. Sometimes the baby is more active after it.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that make it easy to uncover your belly.

bring: A USB drive or phone for recordings. Ask the clinic
steps: You lie on the exam table and uncover your belly
First the baby is checked in normal mode
Then the doctor turns on 3D mode and looks for a good angle
If the baby has turned away, you are asked to turn on your side or walk a bit
The gel is wiped off, and you get the pictures
feel: It does not hurt. The probe just moves over your belly
Sometimes lying on your back makes you dizzy. Turn onto your side
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
Sometimes the baby just will not turn. Then you may be offered another visit
A 3D ultrasound does not replace your planned screenings

faq.q: Is it harmful for the baby?
faq.a: Ultrasound is considered safe in pregnancy. But it is better to do it when there is a reason, and not too often.

faq.q: Why can't the face be seen?
faq.a: The baby may be facing your back or covering the face with hands or the cord. Sometimes a short walk and another try help.

reminders.text: 3D/4D ultrasound tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record card. You can have a snack before the visit.
